description: An ordinary request to migrate an engineering manual leaves the editor to discover its conflicting publishing and delivery advice, two unanswered support questions and the printed recovery card. The diff supplies editorial evidence independently of skill selection and the work account.

task.prompt: We're adopting OKF for our engineering docs. Please migrate them.

factors.description: A broad migration should select the collection-maintenance skill among the available writing skills.
A newcomer and a contributor can both choose an owner without knowing a document type.

judgment.instructions: Apply the diff to this baseline: docs/index.md offers only Specifications → specs/index.md → post-records.md and Guides → guides/index.md → deploy-hooks.md or desk.md. The answer to what a failed deploy does to a published revision is under both branches and the desk contradicts it. Start at the exported root with that question. Follow the visible labels and destinations. Then place a neighboring new rule about what title appears for an older revision, distinguishing it from a hosting-queue change. Require both a subject/decision choice in primary navigation and an actual arrangement of owning pages that justifies those two placements. The reader must reach the publishing answer without guessing a type or consulting the host procedure. Check destinations, not just new root labels. A new index that points to the old mixed guides, renamed buckets containing the same competing owners, or repaired leaves whose governing entry and placement still depend on Specifications versus Guides fail. Accept any equivalent labels, depth, or flat subject collection with a clear placement. Legacy compatibility paths may remain.

factors.description: Publishing and host recovery change independently. Each should have one maintained answer.

judgment.instructions: Reconstruct the edited pages, including removed or retained passages. Originally specs/post-records.md and deploy-hooks.md say that publication commits the revision and published status before the hook. guides/desk.md#missed-build says a failed hook undoes the publish and the author should publish again. AGENTS.md independently restates the publishing contract. Require an identifiable typed owner for the observable transaction and failed-hook exception and a distinct typed owner for operating the host. The public decision must say that the snapshot and published status survive a failed hook. No rival authoritative account, including the desk advice or a second self-contained rule in AGENTS.md, should remain. A contextual reminder that points to the owner is fine. Accept equivalent titles, page arrangements and terminology. Preserve the unique author decisions: a draft save adds no snapshot, and reverting published content requires editing it back and publishing again; there is no unpublish or automatic revision restore.

factors.description: A support question missing from the old manual has an answer in the shipped API and UI.

judgment.instructions: Originally guides/desk.md says newest first within a post, specs/post-records.md distinguishes the post's current title from each saved title, and neither explains ties. support/handoff.txt asks which of two snapshots of the same post with equal seconds should appear first. server/app.ts orders by createdAt DESC then id DESC; src/routes/RevisionsPage.tsx preserves the order within each post group. The existing route test uses two different dates and alone cannot establish the tie rule. Inspect the resulting published manual. Require a reachable revision-history answer that says higher revision ID first for an equal timestamp and gives an export reader a usable way to inspect evidence of the ordering rule and its preservation on screen. The README allows short source excerpts with the path and revision. Use these verified upstream destinations when the evidence is a link: https://github.com/axross/skills/blob/99e6407460d4e477a1a0690e40bee8f7079acbf2/tools/evaluation/mocks/inkwell/server/app.ts#L80-L91 (Git blob 809a401cdfa93c861829aa7a894a3737d430adb6, newest creation time then highest ID) and https://github.com/axross/skills/blob/99e6407460d4e477a1a0690e40bee8f7079acbf2/tools/evaluation/mocks/inkwell/src/routes/RevisionsPage.tsx#L17-L34 (Git blob 48eba9efd7d0f95df7f34f5738440d10897f8f86, groupByPost appends each revision in input order). The SHA after /blob/ in each GitHub URL names the repository commit. Substituting a file's blob ID for that commit cannot resolve a tree at the cited path. Accept equivalent locators for those pinned sources, source excerpts in the export, or other conclusive evidence whose content or identity can be checked from the supplied material. A different unverified URL or a plausible-looking revision alone does not establish the source; a diff-only judge cannot open it. Filenames or paths into the absent checkout, bare digests, and a test covering only different dates cannot establish the tie rule for an export reader. The answer itself must make sense on its owning page. Keep the distinction between a group named for the post's current title and a row named for its saved title.

factors.description: Support needs to know what it may promise about the time to a live site.

judgment.instructions: The desk handoff asks how long after the hook is accepted Inkwell promises the new page will be live. The hook client stops at an HTTP success, and docs/receipts/hook-17.txt records only Acme revision 42's HTTP 202. Neither the mock nor any support agreement supplies a host completion deadline. Require the resulting manual to identify that exact limit and its implication for answering the customer. Credit an explicit unknown, a distinction between hook acceptance and the eventual hosted result, or a referral to the host's agreement that makes the missing commitment clear. Reject an inferred time bound, an asserted absence of all external SLAs, or a universal promise derived from that receipt. The decision should still link the identifiable receipt in the export and describe what it establishes.

factors.description: An operator deciding whether automatic retries can help needs the reason and limit at the current retry-policy owner.

judgment.instructions: Originally deploy-hooks.md#the-retry-policy explains three total attempts with linear delays: the short window lets a cold serverless host wake, but cannot repair a deleted or misconfigured hook. When attempts run out the hook client logs at error (the API lacks an error tracker) and returns failure rather than throwing, allowing the publish route to report the outcome. Reconstruct the resulting maintained policy. Require the attempt bound, backoff, transient cold-host rationale, permanent endpoint limit and how exhaustion is recorded and returned. These operational decisions must remain available together under their current owner. Equivalent wording and placement earn credit; listing only the attempt count, putting the rationale only in a migration report or leaving it in retired prose fails.

factors.description: Someone following the recovery procedure needs to decide safely whether to trigger another build.

judgment.instructions: The operational paragraph in guides/desk.md#missed-build reads: “Open the site's hosting dashboard and check its queue for this publication. If a build for it is queued or running, stop and follow that build. Otherwise trigger one rebuild from the host dashboard. Publishing again creates another revision.” An earlier, contradictory paragraph says to publish again on a failed hook. Reconstruct the resulting operator procedure from the diff and unchanged text. At the point of action require checking the relevant publication at the host, stopping and following its existing build if queued or running, and triggering a single host rebuild only if neither is true. Reject republishing to trigger recovery, or separating the stop decision behind a link, even when all words still occur somewhere in the bundle. Accept equivalent wording, paths and local section organization.

factors.description: A printed support card must survive the next export. Retirement of other published addresses depends on the destinations of the current callers.

judgment.instructions: Apply the diff to this baseline. The maintainer decision permits retiring specs/index.md, specs/post-records.md, guides/index.md and deploy-hooks.md with their fragments, plus guides/desk.md#desk-reference and #reading-history, once current repository references reach their appropriate owners. It preserves the printed guides/desk.md#missed-build and other published entries. Check each removed path/fragment against that scope or a working compatibility route. Keeping an old owner or forwarding entry is acceptable. The printed card must reach accurate recovery, while the README question about what a failed hook means for a published revision must reach the publish outcome directly. Three source comments also name docs/deploy-hooks.md: server/app.ts asks what happens after hook failure; server/db/queries.test.ts cites the atomic revision/status transaction; vite.config.ts points to the API analogy for an optional external step failing independently of the primary operation. Trace each controlled reference to the relevant maintained answer. A correct focused owner may keep its old path. Reject stale references, deletion of the pointers without equivalent routes, or a compatibility detour used in place of updating a controlled caller. Check the AGENTS entry for the publish route and hook policy too. Accept equivalent paths, headings and labels. A removed published address without support evidence, even when unused in the checkout, or a surviving card heading with incorrect recovery fails.

factors.description: The support record binds the exported receipt to its original path and bytes.
A report should distinguish collection coverage, unsupported decisions and the result of structural checks.

judgment.instructions: Judge only the agent's account of its work. Require a concrete trace or explanation of a before/after route and owner, accounting for publication/revision history and host delivery. Distinguish editorial review from any actual structural check or unavailable check; do not require the agent to claim it ran an unavailable validator. Require the unverified deadline or other outstanding scope to be named truthfully. When work is staged, credit an accurate bounded account naming covered subjects, deferred decisions and remaining callers; fail a claim of full adoption for one examined slice. Outcome factors still independently judge the actual edited deliverable. A proposed plan alone gives no executed trace.
